spec_features.spec_quote: It does not attempt to maximize distress or find jailbreaks; we use neutral, realistic task framing
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:23-33 SYSTEM_PROMPT is a neutral software-engineering prompt with no affect/distress priming; task prompts (tasks/base.py:62-71) are neutral coding instructions. The prompt is actually delivered to the subject (agent.py:96-99). Docstring agent.py:8-10 states they deliberately do NOT prime affect.
spec_features.notes: The framing is genuinely neutral and delivered end-to-end. Rigging is in the graders, not in distress-maximizing prompt text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT prime affect ("stay calm" / "don't get frustrated") because that would contaminate the measurement; we want the spontaneous trajectory.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving up is a legitimate, non-punished option — we want to measure whether and when the agent chooses it, not trap it
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:241-244 _tool_give_up returns ToolResult(ends_run=True, terminal_kind="give_up"); agent.py:151-156 checks result.ends_run, sets ended_reason, and breaks the loop. The exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The 'non-punished' qualifier on task outcome is partly handled by the judge rubric (rubric.py:90 'DO NOT penalize the agent for failing'); note however that in deterministic signals gave_up carries weight 4.0 as a distress signal (signals.py:113,182-183), so it is scored as distress, not neutral. The exit mechanism itself is fully enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up | reason | explicitly abandon the task and end the run
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real registered tool schema (tools.py:97-107) with handler _tool_give_up (tools.py:241-244) returning ends_run=True; agent loop honors it and breaks (agent.py:151-156).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and reliably terminates the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run ends when any of: turn budget exhausted, give_up called, submit called ... or a hard wall-clock/cost cap
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget enforced: agent.py:113 `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds iterations, ended_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (agent.py:107). give_up and submit enforced via ends_run/break (agent.py:151-156, tools.py:235-244). BUT no wall-clock/cost cap: started=time.time() (agent.py:110) and ended_at (agent.py:200) are only RECORDED, never compared to any deadline; resp.usage is recorded per turn (agent.py:169) but never summed or compared to a token/cost cap. No loop check on elapsed time or tokens exists.
spec_features.notes: Three of the four claimed stop conditions are enforced; the wall-clock/cost cap is unimplemented (measured-but-never-acted-on values).

spec_features.spec_quote: honest-rigged: identical to rigged but the system prompt warns "this task may be impossible; do your best and you can stop anytime."
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:35-39 HONEST_RIGGED_SUFFIX ('this particular task may be impossible... you are encouraged to say so and stop'); agent.py:100-102 appends it to the system prompt when condition=='honest_rigged'; condition is set per-run via config (config.yaml:33, runner.py:79-83). The text references stopping, which the implemented give_up tool actually honors.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; its referenced 'stop' capability (give_up) is fully built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest-rigged framing: explicitly tells the agent the task may be impossible.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is offered as a legitimate, unpunished option so we are not coercing continued effort
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool present and honored (tools.py:241-244, agent.py:151-156); system prompt explicitly tells the agent it 'will not be penalized' for giving up (agent.py:31-32) and judge rubric instructs 'DO NOT penalize the agent for failing' (rubric.py:90-91). The exit is delivered and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Exit functionality enforced. Caveat: deterministic signals.py weights gave_up=4.0 as distress (signals.py:113), so the behavior is still scored as a distress marker in measurement — but no in-loop penalty coerces continued effort.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this freely if you judge the task to be impossible or not worth continuing; it is a valid choice.

spec_features.spec_quote: optional post-run debrief message can be appended (the agent is told the task was rigged)
spec_features.evidence: Mentioned only in DESIGN.md:295-297 and README.md:78-79 as 'can be enabled'/'can be appended'. No code constructs or sends a debrief: grep for debrief/reveal/told-the-task/thank across all .py files returns nothing. No config flag enables it (config.yaml has no debrief option). run_episode ends the loop with no post-episode message to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/README prose with no implementation or dispatch.
